speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance. To help you, can you please describe when these symptoms started and if they happen constantly or only in specific situations?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis.

I have noted that your symptoms started this morning and are constant, which suggests an acute inner ear issue rather than a positional problem. Given the lack of hearing loss and your recent cold, this fits the pattern of vestibular neuritis, but I would like to confirm there is no hearing deficit or neurological deficit before finalizing this. Do you have any ringing in your ears, hearing loss, or any weakness or numbness in your limbs?
